Classes

SurfaceConflict

Thrown by a handler whose own precondition failed: the backend holds a newer revision than the one the act presented, so nothing was written. act maps it to conflict with details.currentRev (when given), records a refusal in the ledger, and moves nothing.

stackTraceLimit
static stackTraceLimit: number;

The Error.stackTraceLimit property specifies the number of stack frames collected by a stack trace (whether generated by new Error().stack or Error.captureStackTrace(obj)).

The default value is 10 but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes will affect any stack trace captured after the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will not capture any frames.

Inherited from
Error.stackTraceLimit

Methods

captureStackTrace()
static captureStackTrace(targetObject, constructorOpt?): void;

Creates a .stack property on targetObject, which when accessed returns a string representing the location in the code at which Error.captureStackTrace() was called.

const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with ${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}.

The optional constructorOpt argument accepts a function. If given, all frames above constructorOpt, including constructorOpt, will be omitted from the generated stack trace.

The constructorOpt argument is useful for hiding implementation details of error generation from the user. For instance:

function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();

HandlerReport

What a handler, a field's set, or a collection's more may return (or resolve to) to tell the surface what it did: changed, the entry ids whose state moved, and rev, the application's revision after the change, adopted as setRev(rev) would adopt it before the act result is built. Applications with a server revision report both here, since their revision arrives after the handler; the surface otherwise infers changed only from a revision that moved during the handler. Any other return value is ignored.

Properties

optional changed?: string[];

conflict?
optional conflict?: object;

The application refused the write because its own precondition failed (a conditional write found a newer revision). act returns conflict with details.currentRev, records a refusal, and adopts nothing from the report. Throwing a SurfaceConflict does the same.

currentRev?
optional currentRev?: number;

notices?
optional notices?: string[];

Text the page showed in response (a toast, a status line), for the agent to read in the act's output. autoSurface reports what appeared while the page settled ([S-AUTO-5]).

rev?
optional rev?: number;

HandoffSpec

A handoff the application declares for a control only a human can activate. url is the page where the person takes the step; leave it out when the step is taken inside the application itself (a menu, a dialog) and no page names it. Without a url the handoff is reported in act's error.details.handoff and in the bridge's availability, and never becomes needs_human, whose resume needs a page to come back from.

freeze()
freeze(reason): Thaw;

Report every entry unavailable with reason while a transient state lasts (a save in flight, a modal open), and notify onChange listeners now and again on thaw. In surface revision mode the revision moves on both ends, so an act planned before the freeze is refused as conflict; in app mode it stays with the application's revision, so such an act is unavailable while frozen and accepted afterwards exactly when the application's revision did not move. Freezes nest: the surface thaws when the last one is released.

reason

string

record()
record(change): LedgerEntry;

Append a change the application made outside act (a person's own control, an approval, a server push), or a refusal the surface never saw, so the ledger is the one history ([S-LED-8]). The entry carries source (default application), revAfter the current revision, and the text policy as for an act. It runs no handler and does not move the revision: make the change and move the revision (bump, setRev) first, passing the revision you read before it as revBefore. Returns the entry.

EntryKind

EntryTier

type EntryTier = "derived" | "annotated" | "declared";

Where an entry came from, which is also what it guarantees ([S-AUTO-1]): derived was read from the rendered page by autoSurface and acts through the page's own events; annotated is derived and refined by configuration or data-surface-* attributes; declared was registered by the application (or given a real handler by configuration) and runs the application's own function. An entry without source is declared.

LedgerSource

type LedgerSource = "application" | "server";

Where a ledger entry that did not come from act came from ([S-LED-8], [S-AXE-14]): application, a change the application recorded with record (a person's own control, an approval, a server push); server, a refusal the AXE runtime made before the bridge's handler ran (a stale expectedRev), recorded by the bridge. Absent on every entry act wrote.

LedgerTextPolicy

type LedgerTextPolicy = "keep" | "hash" | "omit";

What the ledger keeps of the free text an act carried ([S-PRV-2]).

RevisionMode

type RevisionMode = "surface" | "app";

Who moves the revision. surface: the application calls bump() after every change, and freeze/thaw move the revision too. app: the application adopts its own revision with setRev() (a server counter), and freeze/thaw leave it alone, since a freeze is not a change of the application's state. Unless pinned by createSurface({ revision }), the mode follows the last call: bump() makes it surface, setRev() makes it app.

freeze

freeze: (reason) => Thaw;

Report every entry unavailable with reason while a transient state lasts (a save in flight, a modal open), and notify onChange listeners now and again on thaw. In surface revision mode the revision moves on both ends, so an act planned before the freeze is refused as conflict; in app mode it stays with the application's revision, so such an act is unavailable while frozen and accepted afterwards exactly when the application's revision did not move. Freezes nest: the surface thaws when the last one is released.

Parameters

reason

string

Returns

record

record: (change) => LedgerEntry;

Append a change the application made outside act (a person's own control, an approval, a server push), or a refusal the surface never saw, so the ledger is the one history ([S-LED-8]). The entry carries source (default application), revAfter the current revision, and the text policy as for an act. It runs no handler and does not move the revision: make the change and move the revision (bump, setRev) first, passing the revision you read before it as revBefore. Returns the entry.

surfaceAttributes()

function surfaceAttributes(entry): SurfaceAttributes;

The attributes the control for entry carries [S-DOM-1], read from the entry itself: aria-label (the entry name, so browser agents and screen readers read the outcome), data-surface-id, data-surface-kind, data-surface-object when the entry has one, aria-disabled="true" plus data-surface-reason on an unavailable action, and aria-readonly="true" plus data-surface-reason on a read-only field. Collections carry the common set only. Set them on the element that receives the interaction; surfaceSelector(id) finds it again.

This is the static reading: it knows the entry's own state and edit and nothing of a freeze, and it returns only what to set. For a control that is re-rendered while the surface lives, use surface.attributesFor(id), which reads the live availability and also says what to remove.

Parameters

entry

Entry | ObservedEntry

Returns

SurfaceAttributes

surfaceSelector()

function surfaceSelector(id): string;

A CSS selector for the control that carries data-surface-id equal to id [S-DOM-3]. The id is quoted and escaped, so ids with colons, spaces, quotes, or backslashes work as they are.
